title: After hot start, Florida hits full nose dive after embarrassing loss to South Carolina - CBS Sports
description: Florida struggled to find a pulse against the Gamecocks, who were previously winless in SEC play
body:
Florida struggled to find a pulse against the Gamecocks, who were previously winless in SEC play
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The blueprint's out on Florida this season.And if Jon Sumrall was sick to his stomach after last week's loss at Missouri, Saturday's stunning 38-19 defeat to South Carolina should be vomit-inducing for the first-year coach amid a horrific stretch for the Gators.Since hopping into the top 10 and College Football Playoff conversation last month with an upset over then-No. 4 Ole Miss, the Gators have failed to compete in consecutive losses and will likely fall out of rankings entirely -- this one coming in an inexcusable fashion at home as a double-digit favorite.The Gamecocks' victory was only their third all-time at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium and snapped an eight-game SEC losing skid under hot-seat coach Shane Beamer, who said this week he believes his team was close to turning the corner after blowing leads against Mississippi State and Kentucky this fall.On a day the Gators honored Steve Spurrier and the program's 1966 team with throwback uniforms and a massive pre-game celebration, South Carolina's former head coach and the winningest in school history watched from the box as his alma mater got pushed around by the Gamecocks.
It marked South Carolina's first true road win under Beamer since taking out Clemson in November 2024 and was the Gamecocks' first SEC win in 378 days.After Bailey Stockton opened the scoring for Florida with a 59-yard touchdown reception four minutes into the contest, the Gators looked generally flat for the remainder, lacking the sense of urgency it showed a few weeks ago at home when it demolished Ole Miss. South Carolina was the crisper team and executed well in the passing game after LaNorris Sellers finished with 279 yards and four touchdowns (five total). The Gamecocks never let Florida's rushing attack get going and forced three takeaways after coming into the contest with only two all season, the fewest in the SEC.
Beamer gets voice of supportPrior to kickoff, South Carolina athletic director Jeremiah Donati broke his silence on the angst around the football program and vouched for the players."The guys are playing their butts off. I'm disappointed too," Donati said during a radio interview. "I share that same frustration. When we win, we all win. When we lose, we all lose. I see a lot of good things in this football team. We haven't put it all together. We haven't seen the turnovers like we are used to. "All those things can be fixed. This team is poised for a breakout. Hopefully, we see it here today."
Donati's words lined up with what Beamer has said publicly throughout this difficult stretch to begin the season coming into Week 6 — that based on everything he's been told behind the scenes, he still had the full support of his administration, boosters and others.CBS Sports reported this week that Beamer's future with the Gamecocks wasn't as tenuous as it seemed.Gamecocks squash third-quarter swoonEntering the locker room with a 17-10 lead at halftime, Beamer knew the question was coming, considering his program had blown advantages in conference play several times in recent games.
"We have a long way to go. We've held second-half leads in a lot of games recently, and we have to play a whole lot better in the second half than we have in previous SEC games," Beamer told SEC Network. "We're running the ball, they haven't stopped us, their defense. We're getting takeaways, we're stopping the run – there's a lot to like right now, but we have to go play a better second half.""We ain't gonna hide from it. (Florida) is in their locker room right now telling their players, 'Hey, they haven't played well in the third quarter, let's go get after them.' It's our job to go answer that."The Gamecocks hadn't scored a single point in the third quarter of three previous SEC games this season before Sellers found Donovan Murph in single coverage over the middle for a 26-yard score early in the frame.
This came after Sellers bought time with his legs on 3rd-and-14 and hit Nyck Harbor near the sideline on a drive-extending 35-yard completion.Sellers late scored on a 1-yard plunge to give South Carolina two touchdowns in the decisive quarter as the program notched its first win over a nationally-ranked opponent since the 2024 season.

description: A pair of world title matches, plus the annual ladder matches take place on Saturday night

A pair of world title matches, plus the annual ladder matches take place on Saturday night

        Every year, Money in the Bank sets up months of WWE programming. One man and one woman will earn an automatic shot at any title of their choosing to be used at any moment.The drama and suspense of not knowing when and where the cash-in will happen makes for compelling television, and the ladder matches to determine who has the honor of being Money in the Bank briefcase holder will go down on Saturday in New Orleans.The men's field is loaded on Saturday as it will feature Bron Breakker, Je'Von Evans, Penta, Trick Williams, CM Punk and Kevin Owens. The women's field is just as stacked with Sol Ruca, Lola Vice, Roxanne Perez, Jacy Jayne, Lash Legend and Tiffany Stratton.Two title matches are set for the event, with Roman Reigns defending the world heavyweight championship against LA Knight, and Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch challenging Stephanie Vaquer for the women's world championship in triple threat action. The winners of those matches will have plenty to worry about in the coming days, weeks and months because the winners of the Money in the Bank ladder matches will be hunting for the right moment to cash in their guaranteed shot at a title of their choosing.
With so much action set for Saturday, the CBS Sports wrestling experts sat down to make their picks for who will emerge victorious at Money in the Bank.WWE Money in the Bank 2026 predictionsWorld Heavyweight Championship -- Roman Reigns (c) vs. LA Knight: While I appreciate that the Knight character is one of the only people in WWE who remembers that Reigns' incredible title run was almost entirely the product of endless cheating, he's not ending Reigns' current run as champion. There's a better chance if Reigns loses the belt on Saturday, it's a product of the Money in the Bank winner cashing in than Knight winning the belt. Pick: Roman Reigns retains the title -- Brent Brookhouse (also Shakiel Mahjouri)Bron Breakker vs. Je'Von Evans vs. Trick Williams vs. Penta vs. CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens (Men's Money in the Bank ladder match): WWE have assembled a compelling cast for this year's ladder match. Every man, with the exception of Evans, has a reasonable case for winning the match. Breakker and Williams could launch into the main event scene, Punk has history with the briefcase, plus he and Owens would elevate its status. But after Raw in Mexico City, Penta is my pick. Penta put on a classic against world heavyweight champion Reigns. It helped people visualize Penta as a world champion. Winning Money in the Bank is the easiest way to complete the luchador's bridge between upper midcard and main event. Pick: Penta wins -- Mahjouri
As mentioned by Shakiel, you can make a valid case for five different winners here, though I'd personally eliminate Williams from consideration. I think this comes down to Punk or Owens as the winner since Reigns isn't around enough for Penta or Breakker to be compelling holders, and Breakker is likely tied up with Oba Femi for the foreseeable future anyway. I'll say Owens, simply because I think he would be a fun guy to see strategizing how and when to cash in. Pick: Kevin Owens wins -- BrookhouseSol Ruca vs. Lola Vice vs. Jacy Jayne vs. Roxanne Perez vs. Lash Legend vs. Tiffany Stratton (Women's Money in the Bank ladder match): The women's ladder match really emphasizes how the briefcase can turn a midcarder into a world champion. Excluding Stratton, no woman in the match has won a world title. Legend and Stratton are solid frontrunners, but Perez has a more compelling story to explore. Putting the briefcase on her creates conflict with her Judgment Day teammate Liv Morgan. The stable has been an important part of Raw for a very long time, and this gives them another storyline to dig into. Pick: Roxanne Perez wins -- Mahjouri (also Brookhouse)Oba Femi vs. Bronson Reed: You can't have Femi retire Brock Lesnar and subsequently lose to Reed. It's that simple. Femi must look indestructible until he eventually crosses paths with Reigns, potentially at WrestleMania next year. That's a long time for now, but the payoff works best if Femi remains an unstoppable force. Pick: Oba Femi wins -- Mahjouri (also Brookhouse)
Women's World Championship -- Stephanie Vaquer (c) vs. Becky Lynch vs. Liv Morgan: Vaquer recently regained the belt and WWE doesn't flip titles around quickly very often. The triple threat nature of the match sets up Morgan to be able to cheat in various ways, but I could see Perez's involvement muddying things up if she won Money in the Bank earlier in the night. This is set up for Vaquer to get a win and retain the title in a way that doesn't feel satisfying for Lynch or Morgan as both continue to chase the champion. Pick: Stephanie Vaquer retains the title -- Brookhouse (also Mahjouri)

The veteran receiver could make his Minnesota debut only days after signing with the team's practice squad

                Imagn Images
            
            

    
        The Minnesota Vikings are elevating wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. from the practice squad, according to ESPN. Minnesota makes the move to add depth to its receiver position with star wideouts Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison questionable for their game against the New Orleans Saints.Jefferson was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury, and Addison's hamstring sidelined him in Wednesday's practice and kept him limited in other sessions. If they are out for the game, the Vikings get some backup with OBJ, who joins a WR room that also includes Jauan Jennings.Beckham joined the team this week and, in doing so, reunited with coach Kevin O'Connell, who was the WRs offensive coordinator on the Los Angeles Rams in 2021. With O'Connell, OBJ had 27 receptions for 305 yards and five touchdowns in eight regular-season games and had 21 receptions for 288 yards in four postseason games during their Super Bowl championship run.The Vikings added Beckham following a failed homecoming with the New York Giants. The return didn't live up to the hype and despite making the 53-man roster, he wasn't a key part, or any part, of the offense. He had no targets and no catches in his three games played.
Beckham's most recent previous game action came in 2024 with the Miami Dolphins. He played in nine games, with no starts, with nine receptions for 55 yards and no touchdowns. He played for the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, recording 35 receptions for 565 yards and three touchdowns in 14 games.

body:
The Hoosiers quarterback rallied his team from a double-digit deficit in the fourth quarter, showcasing flashes of what made his predecessor so special
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        When a team finishes a season 16-0 and wins the national title, it's easy to forget about the close calls along the way, but they were there for Indiana last season. The Hoosiers found themselves in close contests on the road against Iowa, Oregon and Penn State during the regular season. In the national title game, they were up against it against Miami.The common thread across all four games was the ability to overcome adversity and make the plays necessary to win. The needle to that thread was Fernando Mendoza. It's why he won the Heisman Trophy, and it's why he went first overall in the NFL Draft. All offseason, the biggest question about Indiana's encore was how well Josh Hoover could fill Mendoza's shoes. On Saturday, in Lincoln, Nebraska, against a team and 90,000 Nebraska fans desperate for their moment in the sun and a return to relevance, Josh Hoover had his Mendoza Moment.It was not a pretty performance overall. In fact, statistically, it was easily Hoover's worst performance since coming to Indiana. Hoover completed only 12 of his 22 passes in Indiana's 20-17 win, as he had to deal with a strong wind blowing through Memorial Stadium all afternoon. It caused him to sail throws to open receivers down the sidelines, and sometimes come up 10 yards short of them. Had he been able to make those throws in the first half, perhaps Indiana never would have found itself in the position it was in when Hoover helped save the day.
To Nebraska's credit, the Huskers did just about everything they had to do in order to pull off an upset. They dominated the ball on offense, running 83 plays to Indiana's 44. The problem was that they couldn't turn those plays into points. Not until Nebraska QB Anthony Colandrea suddenly found himself scampering through the Indiana secondary for a 39-yard touchdown run to give Nebraska a 17-6 lead with 12 minutes left to play.As Nebraska fans collectively lost their minds, and the rest of us suddenly found ourselves wondering if this was really going to happen, Hoover and the Hoosiers' offense stepped back onto the field in the most adverse situation this 2026 team had seen all year. They wasted no time responding.
On the first play of the following possession, Hoover hit Nick Marsh on an RPO for a 75-yard touchdown. Just like that, the air had been sucked right back out of the stadium and replaced with a nervous tension.
You may recall that during the offseason, following critical remarks by his former coach, Sonny Dykes, about turnovers, Curt Cignetti pointed out he'd have something at Indiana he never had at TCU: defense and a run game. Well, the run game wasn't there, but the defense was, and it quickly forced a punt from Nebraska.This time, the response took a little longer, but the result was the same. On fourth-and-2, the Hoosiers went with a play-action pass that mimicked the RPO that led to a score on the previous possession. And like that previous play, Nebraska's defense bit far too hard on the fake. Suddenly, Hoover found himself with not one, but two wide-open options to choose from in Nick Marsh and Charlie Becker. He chose Marsh again, and 44 yards later, the Hoosiers had their first lead of the game.
Neither touchdown was an incredible throw. In fact, they were both pretty easy reads and tosses to make, but the fact that Hoover was able to make them despite all the accuracy issues he'd had in the game, both of his own making and the wind's, showed the kind of short memory a quarterback needs in these spots. It'll also instill confidence going forward that he can make these plays when needed, and that confidence will probably be necessary a few more times.
Things don't get any easier for the Hoosiers next week when they host No. 5 Ohio State.

schema.headline: Josh Hoover gets his Fernando Mendoza moment as Indiana escapes Nebraska scare - CBS Sports

title: Nebraska blows fourth-quarter lead against No. 7 Indiana, extends top-25 losing streak to 31 games - CBS Sports
description: Nebraska missed a golden opportunity to end its top-25 woes
body:
Nebraska missed a golden opportunity to end its top-25 woes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Nebraska was 12 minutes away from ending its 30-game losing streak against top-25 opponents as the Cornhuskers had the defending champions on he ropes. Matt Rhule was on the verge of his first signature win in Lincoln.Then it happened again -- the Huskers let a big win slip through their fingers down the stretch. No. 7 Indiana rallied to score 14 points in 4:48 to win the game, 20-17.As a result of that blown opportunity, Nebraska's losing streak against top-25 opponents has hit 31 games. The Huskers haven't beaten a top-seven opponent since their win over Michigan State in 2015. Rhule is still searching for that signature win that shows real progress in Lincoln.This would have been the program's biggest win since taking down Oklahoma in 2001 -- when the Sooners were the reigning national champions. That's how long it's been since Nebraska has come up with a major win. An entire generation of Husker fans have grown up and graduated from the school without seeing one.
The Cornhuskers were tantalizingly close to changing that on Saturday afternoon, but they wound up with a familiar result. Costly mistakes here and there made the difference as the Huskers failed to execute with the game on the line.Late in the first half, Nebraska got the ball with 6:42 remaining on the clock. It successfully drained that time on a 16-play, 52-yard drive but stalled out on the fringes of the red zone. Kicker Kyle Cunanan missed his 40-yard attempt, and the Huskers came up empty.That miss was ultimately the difference on the scoreboard, but the Huskers made a series of mistakes that produced another gut-wrenching loss.
Immediately after taking a 17-6 lead, the Nebraska defense let Hoosiers receiver Nick Marsh get behind them for a 75-yard touchdown reception. Moments later, on a critical fourth-down play, the Huskers lost Marsh again as he was left wide open for what proved to be the game-winning touchdown.Meanwhile, the offense went ice cold after taking an 11-point lead as Nebraska mustered only 60 yards on 19 plays prior to its final possession.The Huskers will have to keep waiting for a big win, but those opportunities don't come around often, and Nebraska never seems to finish when it gets one.
Decade-long wait continuesThe last time Nebraska beat a ranked opponent was just over 10 years ago on Sept. 17, 2016.The Huskers beat No. 22 Oregon in a thriller, 35-32, with Tommy Armstrong Jr. playing the role of hero. We don't need to delve into the quality of that particular Ducks team because, when you win those games as infrequently as Nebraska, any top-25 win is a good one.This winless streak against top-25 opponents spans across four coaches, going back to the end of the Mike Riley era. Scott Frost -- the favorite son who was supposed to restore the Huskers to glory -- couldn't end it. Mickey Joseph couldn't end it as an interim. Matt Rhule has been unable to end it.
At this point, the Huskers' struggles against top-25 teams seem almost supernatural. It's like the program is metaphysically incapable of finishing in big games. Perhaps someone should try burning sage at midfield in Memorial Stadium.Nebraska should get several more chances to end the drought this season. A road trip to Oregon is on deck, and the Huskers face Ohio State and Iowa in the final two weeks of the season.Can Nebraska get this ranked monkey off its back, or will the losing streak extend into 2027?
More heartbreak for RhuleNot only does Nebraska have a long-running top-25 problem, but its coach does too. Rhule hasn't had much success against ranked opponents lately, dating all the way back to his time at Baylor.In his 134 games as a coach, Rhule has two wins over top-25 teams. Both of those came while he was at Temple, and the last one came 10 years ago against No. 20 Navy.Rhule's record vs. Top 25 teamsTemple:  2-5Baylor:  0-11Nebraska: 0-10Total:  2-26Another issue that has plagued Rhule lately is losing close games -- and it reared its ugly head against Indiana. Rhule is now 2-9 in games decided by four points or fewer at Nebraska, and the Huskers have lost eight straight home games decided by three points or fewer.
For whatever reason, when things get tight in big games, Matt Rhule's teams fall short more often than not. If the Rhule and the Huskers are ever going to hit another level, that has to change sooner rather than later.

body:
An already hostile trip to Anfield gets turned up another level as Enzo Maresca and his squad face the music from the Kop following the Premier League's guilty verdict
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 10, 2026

        Anfield can be one of the most menacing away environments in the Premier League for any team to come to, but this weekend the roof may blow off the stadium as Manchester City come to town. With City having been found to have breached Premier League financial rules by an independent commission, everyone around the league has weighed in with opinions about what should happen. City are appealing the decision. The breaches cover 2009-10 to 2017-18, a span in which Liverpool finished as Premier League runners-up in 2013-14.  That season, Brendan Rodgers' Liverpool were only two points behind Manuel Pellegrini's City, with both teams scoring a whopping 100-plus goals in league play. Anfield never forgets, and the atmosphere could echo 2018, when Liverpool faced Manchester City in the Champions League quarterfinals. Not only was the stadium a wall of red, but so was the approach to it, which Guardiola admitted had an impact on his players. Even if this were a normal match, an undefeated City side would face a hostile atmosphere with Liverpool looking to get back into the top four.How to watch Liverpool vs. Manchester City, oddsDate: Sunday, Oct. 11 | Time: 11:30 a.m. ETLocation: Anfield -- Liverpool, EnglandTV: NBC | Live stream: Fubo TV (Try for free)Odds: Liverpool +170; Draw +260; Manchester City +145Anfield also hasn't seen Premier League soccer in almost a month due to scheduling and a lengthy three-week combined international break. The last home game was a drab draw with Fulham, far enough in the past that fans are ready to see the Reds again, and more than ready to respond to the City decision.1. Can City withstand the pressure?Immense pressure is on Enzo Maresca and the City squad coming into the match to show that the off-field issues are kept there, and the City boss has already called on his away support in a club interview.  "We need to be all together. I said many times the reason why this organisation in the last 15 years was top was because from the owner, the CEO, the sporting director, the manager, players, fans, they are all on the same page. And this is fantastic," Maresca said.  He added that his squad will be ready, but that he needs the fans as well while reiterating that he's calm about the off-field issues. It's one thing to say that, but it's another to back it up while in a hostile atmosphere. Social media has been rife with people's thoughts about City, and while players can ignore that, they won't be able to ignore the fans cheering and jeering from the Kop for 90-plus minutes.  It's a time when the players can come together in support of the club, but with thoughts of what comes next in their heads, a slip-up here could easily become the first step of a spiral. It's hard to predict which way things will go, but that's exactly why it's such an immense match, especially with Champions League soccer around the corner, with Paris Saint-Germain coming to town on Wednesday. City can't ask for a much tougher return from the international break than what they're about to get. 
How will the Liverpool fans react?It will be relentless pressure from the moment City arrive in Liverpool until the moment that they leave. City were already a team that Premier League sides weren't fond of, as success can put a target on your back, but now that even the methods of said success are in question, everyone is out for blood. There may not be a worse place for City to go than Anfield. Even against Manchester United, the economic concerns for Manchester if City were kicked out of the Premier League would loom over the match. The Red Devils may not like their noisy neighbors, but when it comes to Manchester as a whole, things are better when both clubs are successful and competing for league honors.  There's no such buy-in at Liverpool, a club with deep working-class roots. Money being funneled in from the United Arab Emirates is the exact opposite of what the Anfield faithful stand for, which only adds to the animosity that will be at the stadium. How City respond will be critical, as losing here could start an internal spiral, and that's just what the Reds will hope for. Although with punishment looming, it's an open question as to whether City's wins and losses will even matter should massive point deductions, or even expulsion get handed down. Home fixtures at Anfield are already massive affairs, but with the fervor of soccer's return combined with the occasion, this one will be something for the ages. What does the traveling support do?Former City manager Pep Guardiola will be at the Etihad for the Champions League during the week to show his support for his old club and City's continued claim of innocence, but that doesn't mean that the traveling support to Anfield will be just as united. Maresca has asked the fans for their support, but will they be unanimous in that? It's common for fans to voice their displeasure with ownership, but it's also tough to gauge just where City fans are on the charges.  While many fans are maintaining City's innocence, just as current ownership is, public proclamations don't always mirror real life, and if City's away support isn't backing the team, this will be an even longer game than if the players can draw on their away support amid the sea of red that most certainly won't be in their corner. City's owners likely face the possible option of selling the club, depending on what penalties are issued and whether they lose the backing of their most loyal fans is likely to play a roll in that decision.
This is also a litmus test for what City can face on their return home, which could be a rocky one. So much that is not yet known will become clearer on Sunday.

The point guard from Wilmington, Delaware, said she chose to play for the legendary Staley because of her honesty during the recruitment process."From my first time meeting Dawn, to Coach Jo and the staff making me feel right at home, I knew this was where I belonged," Banks, who plays for St. James Performance Academy in Virginia, told ESPN. "They never just recruited me as a player, they recruited me as a person, and they were honest with me about what it would take to get where I want to go. I want to compete for national championships, and I want to be pushed every single day."
This decision caps off a huge summer for the five-star recruit, who won the inaugural WNBA All-Star Shooting Stars competition alongside Shakira Austin and Elena Delle Donne in Chicago and saw her Overtime Select highlight reel go viral, with 8.7 million views and counting.
When speaking with CBS Sports' Isabel Gonzalez in August, Banks said she was looking to commit to a program where she would be allowed to be herself and grow."Definitely somewhere where a coach will allow me to make mistakes, not change who I am, but definitely develop my game," Banks said. title: What's next for Aces? After failed title defense, Jackie Young's free agency looms large - CBS Sports
description: In the closing seconds of regulation on Friday night, after the Las Vegas Aces' 11-point lead had melted away, Chelsea Gray took a hando
body:
In the closing seconds of regulation on Friday night, after the Las Vegas Aces' 11-point lead had melted away, Chelsea Gray took a handoff from A'ja Wilson, drove to her favorite spot on the elbow and put up her patented fadeaway jumper. It floated up, hit the back of the rim and the front of the rim, then spun out, sending the game to overtime. That turned out to be the last gasp for the Aces. They scored six points in the extra frame in an eventual 87-77 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of their semifinal series. The defeat cemented a three-game sweep -- the first time the Aces have been swept since 2020 -- and ended their quest for a second repeat and fourth overall championship in the last five seasons. It was fitting that they lost to the Valkyries, who were led by former assistant coach Natalie Nakase, and had Kiah Stokes starting at center and Tiffany Hayes running their bench unit. Nakase won two titles while sitting next to Becky Hammon, while Stokes was a part of all three of the Aces' title teams before they let her walk in the offseason. Hayes was the 2024 Sixth Player of the Year in her lone season with the franchise. The trio served as a stark reminder of all the talent that has left Las Vegas in recent years and not been properly replaced. At a certain point, you can only ask Wilson, Jackie Young and Gray to do so much. The Aces reached that limit against the Valkyries. 
Wilson was spectacular again this season, winning her third consecutive MVP and becoming the first player in league history to win the award five times. She averaged 26.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.9 blocks on 52.7/40.4/86.4 shooting splits. Her 26.2 points per game were the second-highest single-season scoring average ever -- behind only her own 26.9 points in 2024 -- and gave her a third consecutive scoring title. She also led the league in blocks for the fifth consecutive season. Young, who finished 11th in MVP voting, was also terrific. Her 18.9 points and 6.8 assists were both career-highs, and she was one of four players to finish in the top-10 in both scoring and assists. Gray, meanwhile, had her best season since she broke her foot in the 2023 Finals, and averaged 12 points and 6.7 assists on 44.1/36.5/93 shooting splits. Together, that trio led the Aces to a 31-13 record, the No. 3 seed in the playoffs and a record-setting eighth consecutive semifinal appearance. But in the end, they didn't have enough help, due to a combination of salary cap constraints, poor roster building, injuries and a big bet on Chennedy Carter that failed. 
We'll start with Carter, a former lottery pick who has bounced around the league due to concerns about her conduct, both on and off the court. She got off to an incredible start with the Aces, but they, too, eventually soured on the Carter experience and waived her in July after just 13 games. Without Carter, their options in the backcourt were limited to Loyd, whom they inexplicably gave a three-year, $2.4 million contract in the offseason despite her best days clearly being behind her, and Dana Evans. Loyd averaged eight points on 36.5% shooting and went down with a leg injury in the playoffs. Evans, meanwhile, was limited to 14 games after undergoing knee surgery in the offseason. In the frontcourt, their depth took a serious hit when starting power forward NaLyssa Smith went down with a season-ending non-contact knee injury in August. Their options there were so limited that by the semifinals, Hammon was giving heavy minutes to Kalani Brown, who didn't join the team until late August after Smith's injury. 
Eventually, the lack of support and the pressure of vying for another repeat became too much, both physically and emotionally. In Game 2 of the Aces' first-round series with the Indiana Fever, Wilson had an uncharacteristic outburst at a fan. She received a technical and later apologized to her team for the incident, which became a national conversation. Against the Valkyries, Wilson was limited to 23 points on 41.1% shooting. Young was even worse at 14.3 points on 31.6% from the field. Gray tried her best to support them with 17.3 points a night, but no one else on the Aces scored even 20 total points in the series. "The individual award is going to be what it's going to be," Wilson said of her fifth MVP prior to Game 3. "I love it. I cherish it. I don't take it for granted. But the main goal is always going to be a championship."
"It's just not our time, and I'm OK with that," she said after the defeat. "I'm at peace with the great things we did do. I can't harp on this game too much. I'm just very happy that our team was locked in and we showed up for one another. Obviously, the outcome's not what we wanted, but we're still champions at heart. We're gonna have another opportunity. I guarantee you that."
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Season at a glanceRecord: 31-13 (No. 3 seed)Offensive rating: 112.9 (2nd)Defensive rating: 105.9 (5th)Net rating: plus-7 (4th)Biggest strength: Having A'ja WilsonWilson remains the best player in the world by a wide margin, and has almost single-handedly ensured that they've remained a top-level team despite departures, injuries and an aging supporting cast. Kelsey Plum and Dearica Hamby are gone, Gray isn't the same player she was before her foot injury in 2023, Loyd hasn't been the player they expected, Smith is out for the season, Dana Evans has been limited to 14 appearances and the Carter experiment flamed out. And yet, the Aces won 31 games this season and were one of three teams to finish in the top five in both offensive and defensive rating. With Wilson on the floor, the Aces had a plus-13.1 net rating, and when she was off the floor, they had a minus-11 net rating -- a staggering plus-24.8 net rating differential. Biggest weakness: Lackluster supporting castWilson is the best player in the world, Young is a consistent All-WNBA-level performer and Gray, even at this stage of her career, remains an elite playmaker. But at a certain point, you need more than three reliable players, and the Aces just didn't have that, especially after Carter's departure and Smith's injury. It didn't help that Dana Evans, Jewell Loyd and Stephanie Talbot were all banged up during the playoffs as well. During the regular season, Wilson, Young and Gray accounted for 2,405 of their 4,025 points (59.8%) and 711 of their 970 assists (73.3%). In the playoffs, those ratios were even higher. That trio scored 377 of their 503 points (74.9%) and dished out 79 of their 100 assists (79%). 
Key free agentsJackie Young (unrestricted)NaLyssa Smith (unrestricted)Stephanie Talbot (unrestricted)Cheyenne Parker-Tyus (unrestricted)Biggest question: Can they re-sign Jackie Young? Last offseason, the Aces re-signed Wilson, Gray and Loyd on three-year deals that will keep them in Las Vegas through the 2028 season. Young, on the other hand, only signed a one-year deal, which means she will once again be an unrestricted free agent this winter. Young reportedly did not meet with any other teams during free agency, but her decision to only sign for one year did raise some eyebrows. It's worth noting that she also left Klutch Sports (which represents Wilson, Gray and Loyd) for WME Sports, and dropped Puma to sign a new shoe deal with Skechers. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2019 WNBA Draft, Young has spent her entire career with the Aces and grown into one of the best players in the league alongside Wilson and Gray. Together, they've won three championships, while Young has racked up five All-Star Appearances, the 2022 Most Improved Player trophy and two All-WNBA honors (she'll likely add a third this season). 
Las Vegas' entire offseason will flow from what happens with Young.  Path A: Young re-signsYoung and Wilson are extremely close, and it's certainly possible that Young decides to stay in Las Vegas. She knows the city and the organization. Hammon is one of the best coaches in the league, and playing alongside Wilson guarantees a base level of success. The new collective bargaining agreement instituted revenue sharing so we don't know the exact salary cap figure for the 2027 season, though we can expect it will be up slightly from the $7 million it was at in 2026. Las Vegas was already paying Young a max, so they would have no problem re-signing her. Currently, the Aces have just over $4 million on the books for next season, and re-signing Young to a max would take them well above $5 million.If Young re-signs, the rest of their offseason would consist of trying to fill out a more reliable supporting cast around Young, Wilson, Gray and Loyd. 
Smith and Talbot, who were both starters when healthy, are unrestricted free agents, and it will be fascinating to see what the Aces do there. Smith was excellent after coming over from Dallas in a trade last season, but suffered a season-ending knee injury in August and her availability for 2027 remains in question. Talbot, meanwhile, came on strong after the World Cup, but really struggled prior to the break. She wasn't making much more than the minimum and would make sense to keep around at that price, but the Aces would probably prefer to move her into a reserve role. Re-signing Young to a max and committing over $5 million to six players would leave the Aces with limited flexibility, and building a bench would not be easy, as the franchise is well aware. Path B: Young leavesIf Young decides to leave in free agency, it would be a massive blow to the Aces, especially with Gray and Loyd now in their mid-30s. Young just finished 10th in the league in scoring and fourth in assists after taking on more playmaking responsibility this season, has a proven track record of playoff success and is arguably the best two-way perimeter player in the league. 
Even if the Aces were able to sign-and-trade Young, which they would surely try to do if she indicated she wanted to leave, there would be no way to fully replace what she does for this team. Young's departure would open a max salary slot, and the Aces would assuredly chase one of the other big-name free agents on the market this winter. The two most direct replacements are Kelsey Plum and Kelsey Mitchell. We can pretty safely cross Plum off the list given her history with the franchise. Mitchell, who finished as the runner-up to Wilson in the scoring race and was third in MVP voting, feels like a real possibility, however. Napheesa Collier is the only other true star on the market, and it would certainly be worth reaching out to her. Signing Collier would give the Aces a much different look, but Wilson and Collier would be a dynamite frontcourt to build around. If the Aces replaced Young with Mitchell or Collier, the rest of their work would involve making moves to fill out the supporting cast, just as if Young had stayed. But if, for some reason, the Aces lost Young and were unable to convince any stars to join in free agency, the front office would have to get creative or accept something of a gap year. 
WNBA Draft outlookThe Aces traded their 2027 first-round pick to the Dallas Wings in exchange for Smith ahead of the deadline last season. The move already helped them win a title, and was well worth it even though Smith went down with a season-ending injury in August and is now an unrestricted free agent. The Aces do have their second- and third-round picks (Nos. 28 and 43), but it's unlikely they'll add anyone at those spots who can help them right away in 2027.
